readout_other: Fluorescence tracer (ovalbumin, FITC-dextran) distribution imaging in fixed brain sections, dorsal/lateral brain surface, and cervical lymph nodes; EEG; heart rate, respiratory rate, SpO2; numerical simulation of acoustic propagation and brain temperature from rat skull CT
direction_notes: Sonication did not elicit EEG peaks distinguishable from control (no evidence of neuronal excitation/brain stimulation), while it non-thermally enhanced transport and lymphatic clearance of intracortically injected interstitial solute tracers (a non-neuromodulatory effect).
safety_notes: Histological analysis (H&E, caspase-3, VAF-toluidine blue, GFAP) of sonicated brain regions after a 1-h exposure and 1-week survival showed no tissue damage, apoptosis, ischemic damage or glial infiltration; EEG showed no sonication-evoked neural activation; a 30-min wait after tracer injection prevented the intracranial haemorrhaging previously seen with shorter wait times.

exposures.label: Pulsed FUS to intracortical tracer injection site

target.label: rat cerebral cortex at the intracortical tracer injection site (3 mm lateral, 1 mm caudal to bregma, 2 mm deep)

timing.protocol_description: FUS was delivered stereotactically to the intracortical tracer injection site 30 min after needle withdrawal, for 30 min in the tracer-transport experiment (ovalbumin and FITC-dextran, n=7/group FUS+ and FUS-) or for 60 min in the lymphatic-clearance experiment (ovalbumin only, n=8/group FUS+ and FUS-).

source_quotes.n_subjects: Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats (all male, n = 46) were socially housed (two rats/cage) under a 12 h/12 h light/dark cycle (lights on at 7 AM, of at 7 PM) and were allowed access to food and water ad libitum.

source_quotes.exposures[0].device.manufacturer: A FUS transducer (Ultran Group), operating at a 200 kHz fundamental frequency, was actuated by a sinusoidal electrical waveform from a function generator (Keysight) connected to a 40-Watt linear power amplifier (Electronics and Innovations).

flags.reason: Each rat appears to undergo a single acute, terminal sonication session, but the paper never explicitly states a number of sessions per animal.
30 min (1800 s) was used in the tracer-transport experiment and 60 min (3600 s) in the lymphatic-clearance experiment; both are recorded as a list for this single target/frequency exposure.
Numerical simulation reports in-situ ISPPA and peak-to-peak pressure at the injection site but not an in-situ ISPTA value.

The exact mechanism of the FUS- control condition (e.g., whether the transducer was positioned but left inactive) is not explicitly described; inactive_transducer is inferred from 'the same procedure without receiving sonication'.
